newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT/USLIFE a takeover candidate?
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT/USLIFE a takeover candidate?

text.p: USLIFE Corp is attracting renewed interest as a potential takeover candidate as 76-year-old chairman Gordon Crosby's board term nears expiration and he remains silent on whether he will press the board for another term.
But Crosby, who has been known as a steadfast and vocal opponent of a takeover of the company, would not be eligible for re-election unless he got a board age limit policy revised.
Meanwhile, the chairman has also stopped voicing his opposition to a takeover lately, opting to just keep quiet about the issue instead, sources said.

And with the life insurance industry in the midst of a massive consolidation phase, all this has fueled speculation that the company may now be willing to consider attractive buyout offers, sources said.

Growing takeover speculation has helped drive the shares of USLIFE up about 20 percent from early January levels. USLIFE was unchanged at 41-1/8 at midafternoon on Monday, giving it a market value of about $1.4 billion.

Potential acquirors could include Jefferson-Pilot Corp, American International Group Inc, Conseco Inc, General Electric Co's GE Capital Corp, CNA Financial Corp and ReliaStar Financial Corp, sources said.
Jefferson-Pilot said it regularly investigates possible acquisitions but does not comment on specific companies.
AIG and Conseco declined comment, as did GE Capital. A CNA Financial spokesman said the company is always looking at possible acquisitions or alliances but does not comment on any deals in progress.
ReliaStar said it does not comment on takeover speculation but said it is always looking at possible candidates for a takeover.

USLIFE declined to comment on the takeover speculation as well and also declined to comment on plans for its future leadership. But the company confirmed that under the board's current policy, directors are not eligible for re-election after they reach the age of 75.
The board has already revised the policy twice for Crosby, increasing the age limit first to 70 and then to 75, an industry source said.
The company would not say, however, whether the board would consider increasing the age limit yet again.
Crosby won't be able to avoid the question about his plans for too much longer.

The company's annual meeting is scheduled for May 20 and if he wants to seek re-election, he will be required to reveal his plans in the company's proxy statement, which must be filed with U.S. regulators within the next three months.
"I think we're approaching a decision point for the company," Conning & Co analyst Jeffrey Schuman said.
"Given the high volume of consolidation in the sector, there's speculation about whether this might be a time for the company to consider its strategic options," Schuman said.
Crosby, who has about a two percent stake in the company and has been chairman for 30 years, last year relinquished the post of chief executive officer to Greer Henderson.

The company, which has a large universal and term life insurance business, would be an attractive acquisition for a number of companies, sources said. "They have a quality franchise of products and distributors and it becomes quite attractive to an acquiror," an industry source said.
The company, which has a large presence in New York, would be especially attractive for Jefferson-Pilot and Conseco, which are underrepresented in the state, Schuman said.

Schroder Wertheim analyst Andrew Kligerman, who upgraded the stock in January on the company's takeover potential, said in a research report at the time that the company should sell for at least $44 a share, or 1.3 times estimated book value of about $33.77 a share.
And Schuman said the company could sell for as much as $50 a share but said Conning maintains a neutral rating on the stock.
Analysts may get their next opportunity to question Crosby when the company reports fourth quarter earnings on February 28.
